title: Taste and See That the LORD Is Good

reflections.title: "Taste and see that the Lord is good"

reflect.text: God gave us our physical senses so we can know His goodness in real ways. When we enjoy the rich flavors of daily food or stop to give thanks before eating, we see His creativity and care for us. In worship, especially during the Lord's Supper, tasting the bread and the cup helps our hearts remember Jesus' sacrifice. These physical reminders show us that Christ alone satisfies our deepest spiritual hunger and turns our sorrow into joy.

Tasting God's goodness also calls for personal action. Faith is more than just agreeing with true facts in our minds. It means taking the risk to step outside our comfort zones and placing our entire lives into God's hands. Because our Creator understands us far better than we understand ourselves, we can safely seek refuge in Him and discover His kindness for ourselves.

questions: In what everyday ways can you pause and notice God's goodness around you?
What is one area of your life where God is asking you to step out in faith and trust Him?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for providing for our daily needs and feeding our hungry souls through Jesus. Give us the courage to step beyond our comfort zones and trust You completely. Help us to taste and know Your goodness each day. Amen.

D6.author: Whitney Hopler
D6.work: Taste God's Goodness in Every Meal

reflections.title: "The Lord is near to the brokenhearted"

reflect.text: When we suffer painful losses or letdowns, we often feel like pulling away from the busy world into the shadows. Trying to bottle up our feelings only keeps us trapped in our grief. Yet God does not stay far away when we are hurting. Just as a loving parent sits closest to a sick child who cannot help themselves, God comes near when our spirits are crushed. As F. B. Meyer observed, "brokenness attracts God."

Jesus understands human grief from His own experience, and He grieves alongside us when our hearts ache. We can bring our tears and quiet prayers directly to Him, knowing that even a soft whisper reaches His ears. As we lean on Him and receive support from other believers, God uses our sorrow to build endurance in us and point us to our eternal hope.

questions: What hurt or sorrow do you need to bring quietly to Jesus today?
How can sharing your struggles with other believers help you find comfort and healing?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for drawing close to us when our hearts are crushed and our strength is gone. Remind us that Jesus understands our pain and never leaves us alone in the dark. Use our sorrows to build patient endurance and fix our eyes on the hope we have in You. Amen.

D5.author: Rick Warren
D5.work: 6 Ways to Get Unstuck in Grief

reflections.title: Delivered from All Troubles

reflect.text: Throughout our lives we face many spiritual battles, but we do not face them unguarded. God's angel and His heavenly armies set up camp around those who honor Him. The Lord does not pay us quick, occasional visits when trouble appears. Instead, His protection is permanent, standing watch day and night to keep us from being swallowed up by sudden assaults.

Trusting God does not mean we will escape all hardships. Believers often face sickness, sadness, and opposition. Yet Charles Spurgeon noted that while we may feel the sting of trials, "no great harm shall be done." God keeps our spiritual core safe so that our faith, hope, and love are never broken. In fact, our trials can actually strengthen our patience and stability as we rest under His care.

questions: How does knowing that God keeps a constant watch over you ease your fears?
Looking back at hard times in your life, how has God preserved your faith and hope through them?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You for camping around us and guarding our lives both day and night. When troubles and trials bruise us, protect our faith and keep our hope in You unshaken. Teach us to trust Your faithful deliverance until our journey is complete. Amen.
